questions.prompt: How should the assessment view get its real inputs (system instructions, audio metadata, source text) instead of the current hardcoded sample text?
questions.description: Today assessment_state.raw_text/system_instructions/audio_metadata are never populated from a real notebook anywhere in the TUI — trigger_assessment_grading() falls back to a hardcoded sample string. There's no entry point from notebook_detail (or anywhere) that selects a notebook + generated audio artifact and launches the assessment.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add an action from the notebook detail view: select a notebook that has a generated audio artifact, pull its audio metadata + system instructions + source documents via the existing client/_app layer, and populate assessment_state before entering AssessmentView.

options.label: Wire from notebook detail view (real data, in scope)
Keep sample/manual data entry for now (defer real wiring)

questions.prompt: Which of the TUI visual patterns discussed (entity color-highlighting, topic-weight bar graphs, fact-check pass/fail gutters, chunk density bars) should this goal actually implement, versus keep as the current plain-text panel?
questions.description: The current AssessmentView just dumps chunks + appended metadata text into a scrollable Panel. The richer patterns (ANSI entity colors, bar graphs comparing topic weights, red/green gutters for contradictions) are visual upgrades on top of that.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Implement entity color-highlighting and fact-check pass/fail gutters (highest signal-to-effort); defer topic bar graphs and density bars as a follow-up goal.

options.label: Entity color-highlighting (spaCy entities in source text)
BERTopic weight bar graphs (source vs audio)
Keep it plain text for now, no visual upgrades

questions.prompt: trigger_assessment_grading() in tui/views/assessment_view.py directly instantiates PreprocessingPipeline and calls _app.assessment.generate_assessment, mixing business logic into the view layer (CLAUDE.md's architecture says tui/ should stay transport-neutral-logic-free, delegating to _app/). Should this goal move that orchestration into _app/assessment.py as part of the work?
questions.description: Not required for functionality, but matches the project's stated layering convention (cli/tui -> _app -> client -> rpc).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Yes — move pipeline invocation + background-task orchestration into _app/assessment.py; the TUI view/keypress code should only read state and call an _app function.

options.label: No, leave orchestration in the view for now

questions.prompt: FactCheckAdapter reads its prompt framework from ~/.syncopated/skills/fact-check/sift.skill (a personal machine path, overridable via FACT_CHECK_FRAMEWORK_PATH), and silently returns is_valid=True if that path doesn't exist. Is this external dependency intentional and should it stay as-is?
questions.description: This makes fact-check accuracy dependent on a file outside the repo that most environments won't have, with a silent always-pass fallback that could mask assessment failures.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep the env-var override mechanism, but bundle a minimal default fact-check prompt in the repo so behavior doesn't silently degrade to always-pass when the personal path is absent.

options.label: Bundle a repo-local default prompt as fallback (Recommended)
Leave as-is (personal path, silent pass-through fallback)

questions.prompt: spaCy, BERTopic, and Docling are all optional/soft-fail in the current annotators (missing package -> empty/neutral results, not an error). Should this goal add them as installable extras so the pipeline does real NLP work in dev/CI, or keep them fully optional?
questions.description: Affects docs/installation.md extras and pyproject.toml, and whether tests can assert on real annotation output vs just fallback behavior.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add spaCy (with en_core_web_sm) as a proper extra since it's cheap and central to entity highlighting; leave BERTopic/Docling soft-optional since they're heavier and only needed for the deferred visual patterns.

options.label: spaCy as a real extra, others stay optional (Recommended)
Add all three as required extras

questions.prompt: The view already shows '[Press Enter to confirm or edit score]' but there's no handler for confirming/editing/persisting a score. Should this goal implement that (e.g., saving the human-confirmed score/feedback somewhere), or is it out of scope?
questions.description: In scope would mean deciding where confirmed assessments are stored (local file, db/session.py, etc.) and wiring an Enter-key handler.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Out of scope for this goal — persistence design deserves its own goal once the pipeline + display are solid.

options.label: Out of scope for this goal (Recommended)
